svg.metadata: {"asset_id":"garment-corporate-service-dress-blazer-male","name":"Men's Corporate Service Dress: navy blazer, white shirt and tie, gray trousers (blank nametag)","size_in":{"w":25.522,"h":38.45},"units":"1 user unit = 0.01 in","viewBox":[0,0,2552.2,3845],"size_source":"estimated","size_basis":"Silhouette traced from images/base/male_semi_formal.webp (581x719 px) at 0.0474 in/px, which makes the sleeve-to-sleeve 25.12 in (a men's 40R; the Class A coat at its true scale, make-blues-a.js, is 25.27 in). Trousers are added below the base image's cropped hem. No real garment was measured. Checked against CAPR 39-1 Fig 4.14 (PDF page 87 at 8x) with the figure's 1398 px sleeve-to-sleeve taken as the sheet's 25.12 in (55.6 px/in): the figure's crest centre is 5.53 in from the centre line (Fig 4.12, page 84: 5.37 in), the sheet's pocket and crest centre are 5.49 in from it; the sheet's silhouette, pocket top (12.38 in), crest and lapel overlaid on Fig 4.14 agree within 0.1 in. The lapel is the figure's: its peak is 5.58 in from the centre line at y 6.1 in, the lapel 3.9 in wide, its outer edge 5.35 / 4.44 / 3.97 / 2.84 in from the centre line at y 7.3 / 9.4 / 10.4 / 12.4 in. A rack of 4 miniatures at 11/16 in (2.75 in wide) centred on the pocket has its inner edge 4.12 in from the centre line, so the lapel edge crosses its top rows (1.23 in over the rack at y 7.3, 0.32 in at y 9.4) and clears it from y 10.4 down; Fig 4.12 draws the rack the same way, its top rows against the lapel edge. Moving the pocket out or narrowing the lapel enough to clear the top rows would leave Figs 4.12 and 4.14 (see DECISIONS.md
